scenes.headline: How a search subagent does the frontier model's looking
scenes.sub: Mixedbread's Toast 1, and a benchmark where the score never moved.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Wobble! Toast 1 is Mixedbread's first specialised search agent. Here's how it takes the searching off a frontier model.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Split the work: a specialised agent runs the whole search loop and hands back a package, so the frontier model spends its tokens reasoning.

steps.say: Normally the frontier model searches the corpus itself, turn after turn, filling its own context window.
Instead, it hands the whole search loop to Toast 1, running as a subagent.
Toast 1 searches an index: Mixedbread Search, which it was co-designed with, or one you already have.
It hands back a curated package, and the frontier model spends its tokens reasoning to the answer.

items.say: Inside the loop, it decomposes the query into subqueries,
and curates what matters. How the model does it isn't disclosed: no architecture, no size, no training details.

scenes.title: Harvey LAB, 33 tasks: tokens used
scenes.note: task score 55 in all three runs, on a random subset
scenes.say: On Harvey's legal benchmark, only the retrieval stack changed. Tokens fell from eighty point six million to twenty-three million, and the score stayed at fifty-five every time.

scenes.text: The bet: retrieval is a skill worth its own model, so the frontier model's context goes to reasoning, not navigation.

recap: The frontier model delegates the whole search loop
Toast 1 returns a curated package of evidence
Tokens fell 3.5x on Harvey; the score held
scenes.say: To recap: delegate the looking, get back a package, and spend the tokens on reasoning.
